transcript.text:
"Not working" can mean a few quite different things with a microwave, and they point to very different causes, so let's narrow it down. The most likely possibilities, roughly in order:
• A power problem: the socket, the plug fuse, or (if it's completely dead) an internal fuse or thermal cut-out inside the microwave.
• A control lock (child lock) being on, or the clock needing to be set before it will accept a programme. These stop the buttons responding even though nothing is broken.
• The door not latching properly, so the safety switches won't let it start.
• If it runs (light on, turntable turning) but the food stays cold, that's a heating fault, which is a different route altogether. Quick checks you can safely do:
1. Plug something else you know works, like a kettle or lamp, into the same socket. If that doesn't work either, the socket or circuit is the problem, not the microwave. If it does work, try a known-good 13A fuse in the microwave's plug, as long as it's a standard UK plug you can open. If it's still completely dead after that, the fault is inside the microwave. Don't open the casing to look for a fuse: microwaves store a dangerous charge even when unplugged.
2. If the display lights up but buttons do nothing, look for a lock or key symbol. On many models, holding Stop/Cancel for about 3 seconds turns the lock off. Also try setting the clock, as some models won't start until it's set.
3. Unplug it for a minute and plug it back in. This reset clears some control glitches.
4. Open and firmly close the door. Then put a cup of water in and try one minute on full power. If it won't start, or starts and stops when you touch the door, that points to the door catch or switches. If it runs but the water stays cold, it's a heating fault. To point you the right way: is it completely dead (no display, no light), does it come on but won't start, or does it run but not heat?
display is on, shows the time, and the door light comes on. It beeps when I press buttons but won't start. There's a little L symbol on the display.

That helps a lot. Since the display, clock and light all work, it has power and the controls are alive, so we can set aside a supply fault. I can't confirm what that L means without knowing the make, and it may not be an error code at all. That said, on many microwaves a small L or key symbol is the control lock (child lock) indicator. A lock fits what you're seeing very well: the buttons beep but it refuses to start. It's the first thing to rule out, and it's free. • The control lock is on (most likely, given the L).
• The door isn't being detected as properly shut, so the safety interlock blocks the start. Grease in the latch slots or a worn catch can cause this.
• Less likely, a keypad or control fault. 1. Unlocking varies between makes. Also look for a button marked with a key, padlock or "Lock". Some models need two buttons held together, often Stop plus Start or Stop plus 0. If the L disappears and it starts, that was the whole problem.
2. If the L won't clear, unplug it at the wall for a couple of minutes, then plug it back in. Some locks reset when power is restored. Others stay on, so this is worth one try.
3. If the L clears but it still won't start, unplug it and look at the plastic hooks on the door edge and the slots they go into. Gently clean off any food or grease, and check no hook is cracked. Then plug it back in, close the door firmly and try a cup of water for a minute. If it still beeps and won't start, or only starts when you press on the door, the door interlock switch is the likely cause. That needs an engineer, because it's inside the casing. If you can tell me the make, I can say more confidently what the L means. Your user manual, or a search for the make plus "child lock", will also show the exact unlock buttons.
It's a Samsung. Which button do I press for the lock? I don't have the manual.

I can't confirm what the L means without your exact model, but on many Samsung microwaves the child lock is switched on and off the same way. 1. With the door shut, press and hold the Stop/Eco button (on some models it's just Stop or Stop/Cancel, usually marked with a square or a cross) for about 3 seconds, until it beeps. If the L goes out, that was the lock. Put a cup of water in and try a minute on full power.
2. If nothing changes, look for a button with a padlock or key symbol, or the word Lock, and hold that for 3 seconds instead.
3. If the L still won't clear, unplug it at the wall for a couple of minutes, plug it back in and try step 1 again. If the L clears but it still beeps and won't start, the next suspect is the door not being detected as shut. If it still won't start, or only starts when you press on the door, that points to the door interlock switch. That one needs an engineer. Samsung puts its user manuals on the Samsung UK website if you want the exact steps.
ok tried holding the stop button for 3 secs, the L went away and it works now

Good news: that L was the child lock, so nothing was broken. It simply stops the microwave starting while still letting the buttons beep. To stop it catching you out again, avoid resting a hand on or holding the Stop button for more than a second or two, for example when wiping the front or cancelling a programme. That's the usual way it gets switched on by accident. Is there anything else I can help with?

Not heating (magnetron/high-voltage fault) while it otherwise runs (low)
